preconditions.description: The number of nodes n must be between 2 and 400 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(-1000 <= xi <= 1000 and -1000 <= yi <= 1000 for xi, yi in nodes)
preconditions.description: Each node's coordinates (xi, yi) must satisfy -1000 ≤ xi ≤ 1000 and -1000 ≤ yi ≤ 1000.
The number of nodes provided must match the given n.
All nodes must have distinct coordinates.

postconditions.description: The output must be either '-1' indicating impossibility or a non-negative float representing the total length of the arcs.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(yu > yv for u, v in arcs if (u, v) in arcs)
postconditions.description: If a binary root tree is possible, all arcs must be directed from top to bottom (yu > yv).
If a binary root tree is possible, the number of arcs must be n - 1.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(u in nodes and v in nodes for u, v in arcs)
postconditions.description: If a binary root tree is possible, all endpoints of arcs must be valid nodes.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(len(children) <= 2 for children in adjacency_list.values())
postconditions.description: If a binary root tree is possible, each node must have at most two children.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(visited for visited in visited_nodes.values())
postconditions.description: If a binary root tree is possible, all nodes must be visited in the constructed tree.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or return_value == sum(((nodes[u][0] - nodes[v][0]) ** 2 + (nodes[u][1] - nodes[v][1]) ** 2) ** 0.5 for u, v in arcs)
postconditions.description: If a binary root tree is possible, the return value must be the sum of the Euclidean distances of all arcs.
